correctness.rationale: The missing-branch formula A=J-R and Q=RP are exact under the source matrix convention. Decompose constants plus zero-sum subspace to get spectrum of J-Q. Each permutation cycle gives roots of unity; delete one constant root, scale by m. The exponential permutation cycle index gives the rational exact incidence products. The explicit N=4 matrix and the convex-hull strictness argument supply a rigorous contradiction. The standalone finite verifier returns VERIFY_OK for all 4!..7! shuffles, but the proof does not depend on exhaustion.

originality.rationale: The original preprint supplies the transfer reduction, root-of-unity criterion and sharp m=N−1 mixing bound, but poses the convex-hull restriction as Conjecture 2.4.1. The constructed order-(N−1) points are outside that conjectured polygon, while no source inspected supplies the stated all-shuffle phase-spectrum formula or exact incidence fractions. This is a new implication beyond the prior generic bounds under the available evidence, with unindexed priority risk.
residual_risks: The original article informally calls Λσ isolated second eigenvalues even though its literal definition includes points on the essential spectral radius; the counterexample must be read using its precise formal definition, not a modified strict-isolation-only claim.
A separately indexed or unpublished equivalent permutation-cycle computation may exist; no absolute historical-priority certification.
No characterization of non-Markov essential spectral points is attempted.

value.rationale: An explicit conjecture about spectral phase geometry is refuted in every eligible N≥4 by a natural family, while every possible peripheral Markov eigenphase and its exact permutation frequency are classified. This resolves a motivated structural gap in the source study, not merely a routine inequality, and differentiates phase distributions even though all shuffles share the already-known rate 1/(N−1).
